# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

Actually the three monkeys: Deaf (can see bomb, can't hear), Mute (can read manual, can't speak), Blind (can touch bomb, can't see). 

The Mute — can they see? The Blind can't see. The Deaf can see. What about Mute? The Mute reads the manual — reading requires sight. So Mute can see. And Mute can hear? Mute can't speak but can hear presumably.

So:
- Deaf: sees bomb, sees gestures, can't hear.
- Mute: reads manual, can hear, can see, can't speak.
- Blind: touches bomb, can hear, can speak, can't see.

Now the speaking order: Mute, Blind, Deaf. So this round:
1. Mute speaks/gestures first.
2. Blind speaks/gestures second.
3. Deaf (me) speaks/gestures third.

What I received: Mute gestured to me [✊ 👉 ✌], Blind gestured to me [👋 ✊].

But wait — these are "new arrivals" at the start of turn 1. Since I'm last in the order, Mute and Blind have already gone. Mute's gestures reach me (I can see). Blind's gestures reach me (I can see). 

But hold on — Mute's speech reaches Blind (who can hear) but not me. Mute's gestures reach me and... does Mute's gesture reach Blind? No, Blind can't see. So Mute's gesture only reaches me.

Blind's speech reaches Mute and me? Blind can speak. Blind's speech reaches everyone who can hear: Mute and... me? I'm Deaf, I can't hear. So Blind's speech reaches Mute only. Blind's gestures reach me and Mute (both can see).

I need to communicate this to Blind (who can touch the bomb) and Mute (who has the manual).

Wait, my speech: "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it." So both Mute and Blind hear my words. Good — I can describe the bomb in words to both of them.

But there's a catch: "A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never read it out." The colours have names (purple, green, blue, yellow). The display shows 0. So I can say all of this.

So my best move: speak to both Mute and Blind describing the bomb: display 0, light purple, wires 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow.

Hmm, Mute can't speak. So Mute can only gesture. Blind can't see gestures. So Mute cannot communicate with Blind at all?! Mute can't speak, and Blind can't see gestures. So Mute → Blind is impossible directly.

Wait, but Mute can hear Blind's speech. And Blind can hear Mute's... no, Mute can't speak. So how does Mute tell Blind anything? Mute would have to gesture, but Blind can't see.

Hmm, so the only way Mute communicates to Blind is through me (Deaf) as intermediary? But I can't hear Mute's speech... wait, Mute can't speak anyway. Mute gestures to me, I see it, then I speak to Blind. That works!

- Blind → Deaf: gestures (Deaf sees)

Hmm, these could be attempts to establish a code. But I have no way to know. Let me just describe the bomb and ask for clarification.

Let me send this to Mute (who can then figure out the manual's instruction and gesture it to me, and I relay to Blind).

Also send to Blind so they know the layout.

Let me write my calls.

Actually, I want to be careful about the "to=" parameter. If I name "mute", only Mute receives. If I name "blind", only Blind receives. If unnamed, everyone who can perceive receives.

Let me send:

And maybe gesture to Mute to acknowledge.

Hmm, but actually, should I be more careful? The gestures I received might contain info I'm missing. Let me just also mention them.

Actually, let me keep it simple and clear. I'll describe the bomb to both.

Let me also think: is there any risk in speaking? No, speaking is safe.

Let me write the response.

I'll speak to mute and blind, and gesture to mute (a simple acknowledgment or maybe repeat). Actually, gestures to Mute might not be needed. Let me just speak.

- LIGHT: purple

**Who can reach whom:**
- Mute can read the manual but can't speak, and Blind can't see — so Mute cannot reach Blind directly. Mute can only gesture, which only I can see. So I am the bridge from Mute to Blind.

So the critical path: I must get my visual reading (light colour + wire colours) to Mute, who holds the manual and can determine the correct action, then Mute gestures the instruction to me, and I speak it aloud to Blind, who can actually work the bomb.

The gestures I received (Mute: ✊ 👉 ✌; Blind: 👋 ✊) have no established meaning yet — nothing has been defined, so I can't safely interpret them. I'll report my concrete observations in words, which both Mute and Blind can hear.
